summary:
New Hampshire is a state of the United States. Passports, visas, entry screening and federal facilities are governed by federal law; the findings below concern the state layer.

State anti-discrimination law has covered gender identity in housing, employment and public accommodations since June 2018. Coverage was extended to health care, public accommodations and jury selection effective 1 January 2020, and to public schools effective 17 September 2019, with the anti-bullying statute reaching gender identity and expression, including cyberbullying. Sexual orientation has been protected in public accommodations, housing and private and public employment since 1998.

Hate-crime penalty enhancements for offences motivated by gender identity took effect on 15 October 2019; sexual orientation has been covered since 1991. The gay and trans panic defence was abolished effective 1 January 2024, following passage in June 2023.

Enforcement of the state civil rights statute is documented. On 17 July 2026 the Merrimack County Superior Court found that a Concord man had violated the New Hampshire Civil Rights Act by striking a transgender woman.

GLAAD's 2025 national incident census recorded 72 anti-LGBTQ incidents in New Hampshire, the second-highest raw count of any state after California (198) and ahead of Texas (66), Ohio (50) and Washington (50). The census ranks by raw count and publishes no per-capita denominator, so the figure does not by itself establish New Hampshire's incident rate relative to larger states.

Identity documents are asymmetric. A New Hampshire birth certificate can be changed to reflect a different gender only on proof of sex reassignment surgery, legal in the state since 1990, together with a certified court order stating a "sex change," an application form, a photograph and fees. A reform bill was vetoed in July 2019 and the surgical requirement remains. Driver's licences have offered male, female and X markers since 1 January 2020, implemented in August 2021; the X marker is not available on birth certificates.

Care rules for minors have tightened. Laws passed on 18 July 2024 banned gender-affirming medicine for minors and, from 1 January 2025, banned reassignment surgery for transgender minors while retaining it for intersex people and circumcisions. House Bill 377 and House Bill 712, passed in August 2025 and effective January 2026, ban puberty blockers, hormone therapy and chest surgery for under-18 gender-affirming care, with a grandfather clause for treatment already under way as of 1 January 2026, disciplinary action against providers who violate the ban, and a right to sue. Those August 2025 laws removed access to gender-affirming care for transgender youth even where a physician judged it medically necessary.

The same July 2024 package barred transgender girls from girls' sports in grades 5 to 12 from 19 August 2024, with a birth certificate required to establish eligibility. A fourth bill in that package, which would have permitted discrimination against transgender people including adults, was vetoed. In August 2024 the state Supreme Court ruled 3-1 to protect transgender students in schools on privacy and autonomy grounds, and a judge granted a temporary stay of the sports ban pending investigation and appeals.

Marriage between two people of the same sex has been legal since 1 January 2010, following civil unions from 1 January 2008. An April 2021 Supreme Court ruling recognised adultery in such marriages, reversing the 2003 Blanchflower rule.

Same-sex sexual activity has been legal since the sodomy repeal of June 1975. The age of consent is 16 regardless of sexual orientation, and 18 where one party is under the care, guardianship or authority of the other.
tangentialFactors:
A 2022 Public Religion Research Institute poll found that 88% of New Hampshire residents supported discrimination protections covering sexual orientation and gender identity, with 11% opposed.

Wikipedia's article on LGBTQ rights in New Hampshire states that the state "became regarded as the least safe New England state for transgender citizens" after the August 2025 care restrictions and other changes to transgender protections. The characterisation is attributed rather than measured.

Two earlier measures failed. A 2022 bill that would have required schools to disclose students' gender identities died after a veto threat, and a 2022 attempt to repeal the conversion therapy ban died in the House.
localsOnly:
State employment and contracting: a 30 June 2016 executive order prohibited discrimination on the basis of gender identity and expression in public employment, state programmes and contracting. Sexual orientation was explicitly listed in expectation-of-privacy legislation effective 1 January 2025.

Schools: the July 2024 package allows parents to opt their children out of instruction on gender identity or expression. Anti-bullying law covers gender identity and expression, including cyberbullying, and has covered sexual orientation since the 2019 extension.

Health coverage: the state's ban on Medicaid coverage of transition surgery was lifted on 20 October 2017. Conversion therapy on LGBT minors has been prohibited since 1 January 2019, after passage in 2018.
outOfScopeNotes:
The operative status of the sports ban is unresolved in the sources consulted: a judge granted a temporary stay pending investigation and appeals, and the outcome of that process is not recorded.

The incident census ranks by raw count and publishes no per-capita denominator, so the ranking does not establish a per-capita rate for New Hampshire or for any other state.

Whether the 2025 restrictions on gender-affirming care for minors have been enjoined, and their status on any given date, is not established by the sources consulted.

The requirement of surgery and a court order for a birth certificate change is recorded as remaining in force after a July 2019 veto; no later amendment is recorded.
